title: Rotations and Break-Glass Cheatsheet
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact operational cheat sheet for secrets vaulting, rotation, break-glass handling, and the evidence automation pipeline that proves rotations happened. Meant for on-call security, SREs, and devs who own credentials. Keep this page as the quick reference; longer runbooks live on Confluence (see linked artifacts).

Scope:
- Applies to all service credentials stored in HashiCorp Vault (kv-v2 and transit) and KMS-managed keys used for signing.
- Covers rotation cadence, automated proof collection (evidence artifacts), SIEM export fields, and emergency break-glass flows.
- Excludes user-facing password resets (handled by IAM/IDP team).

High-level flow (typical rotation):
1) Rotation trigger: scheduled job (cron on infra repo) or manual request (SEC JIRA ticket).
2) Pre-checks: confirm consumer services have pull-ready deploy windows and feature flags for canary rollout.
3) Perform rotation in Vault (kv write / kv/… or transit rotate).
4) Update dependents (k8s secrets, config stores) via controlled rollout.
5) Post-checks: smoke requests, metric validation, audit event collection pushed to SIEM.
6) Emit evidence bundle to S3 and attach to JIRA ticket.

Quick commands (common patterns) - replace placeholders: 
- Read secret metadata (kv-v2): vault kv metadata get secret/path/thing
- Rotate: vault kv put secret/path/thing value=@new_value.json --cas=0  (use automation instead of manual where possible)
- Transit key rotate: vault write -f transit/keys/service-key/rotate
- Revoke token (break-glass): vault token revoke <token-id>
- List leases: vault list sys/leases/lookup

Vault naming conventions (enforced):
- path: secret/{env}/{team}/{service}/{credential}
  e.g., secret/prod/eng-serving-runtime/redis/primary
- metadata tags: owner=team-name, expiry=YYYY-MM-DD, rotation_policy=semi-annual

Rotation cadence (recommended):
- Short-lived API keys (internal): 7 days
- Service tokens (longer lived): 90 days with automatic rolling leases
- Static TLS cert private keys: annual or on-suspected-compromise
- Database passwords: 30 days or on IAM change

Evidence automation (what we collect automatically):
- rotation_manifest.json (who/what/when)
- vault_audit_slice.ndjson (filtered audit log entries for the operation)
- deploy_rollout_log.txt (k8s rollout outputs + checks)
- smoke_test_results.json (smoke endpoints + request IDs)
- signer_check.txt (if transit key rotated, include public key fingerprint)
All artifacts are zipped and stored under s3://redwood-security-evidence/rotations/YYYY/MM/DD/{ticket-id}/bundle.zip and a pre-signed link is attached to the JIRA ticket.

SIEM export mapping (fields we push for each rotation event):
- time: ISO8601 timestamp
- host: vault-node-identifier
- actor: principal (user/service)
- action: vault API path + verb (e.g., kv/put, transit/rotate)
- resource: vault path affected
- request_id: vault-request-id
- result: success | failure
- correlation_id: jira_ticket or deploy_id
- evidence_url: s3 presigned link
Example ndjson line: {\"time\":\"2024-11-15T20:12:03Z\",\"actor\":\"infra-bot@redwood\",\"action\":\"kv/put\",\"resource\":\"secret/prod/eng-sre/monitoring/api-key\",\"request_id\":\"req-abc123\",\"result\":\"success\",\"correlation_id\":\"SEC-1234\"}

Audit log schema (short):
We push Vault audit frames into SIEM as flattened JSON. Important fields to keep: timestamp, entity_id, client_ip, request_path, method, status_code, response_size, auth_method, token_policies. Keep minimal PII.

RBAC v2 notes (application to secrets):
- Avoid team-wide root tokens. Use role bindings per service account. RBAC v2 policy templates: 
  - read-only role (secrets:read) scoped to path secret/{env}/{team}/{service}/*
  - rotate role (secrets:rotate) includes kv/create, kv/update, transit/rotate for a specific path
  - emergency-role (break-glass) with time-limited bindings via TTL (max 4h) and MFA requirement
- Enforce least privilege and use groups mapped from IDP.
- Periodic policy review every 90 days (automate check: infra script compares policies with owner tags).

Break-glass scenarios (common):
1) Immediate compromise suspected (public disclosure, leaked token):
   - Create SEC JIRA ticket, tag P0, notify #sec-ops and #oncall-sre in Slack.
   - Revoke affected tokens: vault token revoke -prefix <token-prefix> or revoke-by-lookup for lease ids.
   - If secret is used by many services and immediate revocation causes outage, perform staged replacement: rotate value in Vault then update one canary service to validate, then cascade.
   - Capture evidence: snapshot of vault audit frames (use vault-audit-collector script) and push to evidence S3.
   - If root cause is IAM misconfig, roll roles/policies and rotate admin keys.

2) Emergency access required (operator needs temporary escalated access):
   - Use emergency-role flow: request via internal portal which creates a short TTL binding and issues ephemeral token (max 4 hours). Portal requires approval from two on-call approvers.
   - Always attach reason and jira ticket id.

Post-incident checklist (attach to ticket):
- Evidence bundle uploaded and link added to JIRA.
- Audit frames for the window analyzed and SIEM rule updated if necessary.
- Affected policies rotated, and owners notified.
- Lessons learned doc (short) created and retro scheduled.

Automated proof pipeline (implementation notes):
- Cron job in infra repo triggers rotation-runner (k8s job).
- rotation-runner does: pre-checks -> call vault API -> update k8s secrets via sealed-secrets operator -> run smoke checks -> collect audit frames via /sys/audit -> assemble bundle -> upload to S3 -> post JIRA comment via API.
- Failure modes: rollback if smoke tests fail; if upload fails, alert #sec-ops and attach local CI artifact to ticket.

Smoke tests (examples):
- For datastore: simple read/write test with tracing headers, record request_id in evidence.
- For signing: verify signature of test payload with new key and compare fingerprint.

Notes to self / unresolved:
- We still need an RBAC v2 automated scanner to detect overly broad policies (TODO: infra issue).
- Should add TTL enforcement for emergency-role creation in the portal (limit to 1h for high-risk scopes).
- Document how to handle third-party integrations that do not support short-lived secrets.

References and quick links:
- Confluence: Secrets Lifecycle Overview (linked_artifacts)
- Jira demo ticket: JIRA-SEC-1234 for a recent rotation test (refer to evidence in S3)
- Infra PR implementing rotation-runner: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/417

Contact: Aisha Patel (sec-engineering lead) — ping in Slack @aisha.p or #sec-ops for urgent follow-up.

-- End quick cheat sheet (expand on Confluence for full SOP)
